newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle tumble for limit loss at close.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle tumble for limit loss at close.

text.p: Long liquidation intensified late as December CME live cattle futures tumbled for a limit loss of 1.500 cents per lb and other months finished sharply lower. Feeder cattle followed to also end lower, traders said.
December live cattle ended limit down at 66.300 cents and October finished sharply lower, off 1.375 cent at 72.125 cents. Other months were down 0.825 to up 0.050 cent.

Long liquidation, rolling out of longs in October ahead of first notice day and pressure attributed to apparent toppy action in cash markets weighed on prices from the start and took futures down into technical sell stops, traders said.
"The big open interest and first notice day coming up Monday" caused the selling pressure, said Karl Skold, Director of Research for Frontier Risk Management.
Skold added that cash cattle was just steady and there was no reason for longs to hang on to futures. Charts look toppy "and that's fueling the negative attitude," he said.

December fell the limit the last couple of minutes when stop loss selling intensified under 66.500 cents. Buying by E.D.& F. Man, Rosenthal and RBH failed to offset the heavy amount of sell stops. Nearly 700 contracts remained offered at the limit down in December at the close, pit sources said.
Pit sources also cited spreading of long February/short October by Prudential Securities early and sell stops touched off under 72.600 cents.

In live cattle options, general selling of 66 and 68 December calls were cited on the late futures break. Cargill Investor Services sold December 70 calls and there was some buying of December 68 puts, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures continued to follow the lead of live cattle and moved down to or near day's lows late. Paring of early losses in corn futures also weighed on sentiment, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.15 at $63.94 per cwt.

E.D.& F. Man sold and Lind-Waldock bought while Stone Traders was on both sides of the market late. Cargill Investor Services spread long October feeders/short February live cattle and long March feeders short August live cattle, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle closed 0.725 to 0.125 lower with October off 0.575 at 63.600 cents.
